implementation_notes: JavaScript has no scope object: Promise.all joins a fixed set and rejects with the first rejection, but rejecting does not cancel the siblings (MDN), so every child must receive an AbortSignal from one AbortController that the scope aborts in finally; await Promise.allSettled(...) after the abort when the scope must not return before the children have actually stopped. Cancellation is cooperative - children must observe signal.aborted or use APIs that consume the signal - and the try/finally is what keeps the scope's guarantees on error paths.
pitfalls: After Promise.all rejects, the sibling promises keep running unless the AbortController is aborted and their later rejections are handled.
Aborting is cooperative: a child that never reads signal.aborted runs to completion, so the scope's exit is not automatically the child's end.
Timers, streams and listeners need explicit teardown in finally; aborting a fetch does not close a WebSocket or clear a setTimeout.
Fire-and-forget async calls made inside the scope escape it entirely - every child must be represented by a promise the scope joins.
